purpose: Bind the v1 one-shot orchestration-host plus pure-evaluation-core floor, while keeping future residency parked and runtime ambient-authority denial explicitly NOT DISCHARGED.

resolves.B-R1V12-01: RESOLVED — ExecutionId is allocated by the host at attempt admission and INJECTED as metadata; the core never mints it; LN-13 asserts distinct ids over identical inputs yield identical EvidenceDigest.
resolves.B-R1V12-02: RESOLVED — boundary-aware rules: direct ambient imports forbidden, port calls permitted, core analysed TO THE PORT BOUNDARY, each production adapter conformance-tested separately. The runtime half is LN-12, unimplementable, and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED.
resolves.B-R1V12-03: RESOLVED BY CHOOSING A FACTORING — orchestration host runs effectful and provider stages and passes a sealed StageInput into a pure evaluation core, which never calls back out. This is the factoring C-2's effect taxonomy already implies.
resolves.B-R1V12-04: RESOLVED — three suites (core, host, storage) with the rule that a failure in one may not be read as evidence about another. R-1(1) closes on the CORE suite alone.
resolves.B-R1V12-05: RESOLVED — no exhaustiveness claim. Four instruments are named with what each cannot see; unmodelled dynamic and native paths are TCB-ACCEPTED or denied by construction, never claimed as analysed.
resolves.B-R1V12-06: RESOLVED — CoreCompletion is a typed union (completed / incomplete / cancelled / faulted) reusing the fact-plane deficiency and D9 fault vocabularies. The core never seals or maps a termination.
resolves.B-R1V12-07: RESOLVED — the v1 floor is one-shot host plus pure core. Resident/autostart/default/multi-project modes are parked outside v1 and require measurement plus an explicit later scope change.

decisionDependencies.claim: v1 selects one-shot host + pure core; future resident topology is parked outside the implementation scope
contention resolved by busy-timeout, idempotent insert, write-then-link — integrity, not liveness
warm state is an acceleration, never an evidence authority
equality only for deterministic producers under identical identities and exact Coverage
LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT is a typed operational termination distinct from corruption

executionCoreBoundary.definition: The execution core is a pure evaluation function: it takes a sealed StageInput / ObservationSet (already derived by the host), a validated Plan fragment naming rule-evaluation and policy-evaluation stages, and host-injected AttemptMetadata, and returns a CoreCompletion. It does NOT take an unsealed Snapshot for fact derivation, does NOT produce a SealedRun, does NOT seal, publish, or map HostTermination.

inside.why: C-2 declares rule-evaluation holds no effect authority; this is the pure core's job.

inside.authority: policy evaluation over findings + exactCoverage + Plan policy identity
inside.why: Policy is a pure total function of sealed inputs; the core returns the policy outcome so the host need not re-evaluate.

inside.authority: budget accounting for core-executed stages only
inside.why: Budgets for rule/policy stages are Plan inputs; exhaustion is Coverage the core must produce.

outside.why: InvocationPlan work (c2-plan-stage-schema.v2). The core receives resolved identities.
Grants are fixed in PlanId before the core runs. A core that could grant could escalate.
Probe and scanner execution is supervised OUTSIDE the core. Placing a process supervisor inside would give the core spawn authority, defeating LN-12.
Host concerns. Their absence from the core is what makes lifetime-neutrality meaningful.

injectedNotAmbient.resolution: INJECTED by the host. Never minted by the core. Excluded from EvidenceDigest.
INJECTED as an immutable value map. The core cannot look anything up.
INJECTED pure value: remaining budgets and a meter that only decrements counters. No threads, processes, clocks, or entropy.
INJECTED and bounded. A no-op sink must be valid and must not change results.

exhaustiveness.why: v1.1 asserted CoreDeps exhaustive, which A2 correctly rejected: a field list cannot prove the absence of unlisted ambient access. Exhaustiveness is now the CONCLUSION of LN-11 and LN-12, not a premise.

coreApi.signature: evaluate(stageInput: SealedStageInput, deps: CoreDeps, attempt: AttemptMetadata) -> CoreCompletion

attemptMetadata.rule: Injected, never minted. Excluded from EvidenceDigest by construction. No entropy field.

fields.planStageIds: non-empty ordered immutable Plan stage identity list

conformanceTests.assert: Two sequential evaluations in one process produce identical results to two in fresh processes.
The core package declares only port dependencies; no direct ambient import appears in its dependency policy.
The host releases every resource on every exit path, including cancellation.
Cancellation mid-evaluation returns a typed cancelled CoreCompletion, not an exception.
A provider fault is contained and returned as faulted, never as a finding.
A warm and a cold store carry byte-identical authoritative ledger, baseline, evidence and derivation inputs, differing only in disposable acceleration entries.
Two concurrent writers never produce a corrupt, partial or lost publication.
Crash during publication leaves the ledger recoverable; orphans are abandoned, never sealed as success.
A contender may return a typed busy timeout after bounded retries; integrity is guaranteed, liveness is not.

A resident host produces no Run a cold host could not produce identically (EC-3). COMPOSITION: compares resident vs cold host with byte-identical core and storage held fixed by construction; failure is not attributable to host suite alone.
Import/call closure over the core package reaches no direct ambient authority, analysed TO THE PORT BOUNDARY, with the boundary and its limits stated.
A core attempting a denied capability at RUNTIME is refused and the attempt recorded.
conformanceTests.note: B-R1V12-02/05. Static closure cannot prove runtime denial, and no restricted runtime exists. Declared, not discharged.

conformanceTests.assert: Varying ExecutionId over identical semantic inputs produces byte-identical EvidenceDigest, and every ExecutionId is distinct across attempts.
conformanceTests.note: B-R1V12-01. Both halves matter: distinctness makes orphans nameable, digest-invariance makes retries comparable.

conformanceTests.assert: Every CoreCompletion variant is reachable, and no variant seals a Run or maps a termination.

identityOwnership.why: B-R1V12-01, critical. v1.2 had the CORE mint an identity that admission owns, so retries and concurrent identical requests collided.
identityOwnership.rule: ExecutionId is allocated by the HOST at attempt admission (C-2 level 2) and INJECTED into the core as AttemptMetadata. The core never mints it and has no entropy source.
identityOwnership.mustNotAffect: EvidenceDigest. Two attempts with different ExecutionIds over identical semantic inputs MUST produce byte-identical EvidenceDigest.
identityOwnership.whyBoth: ExecutionId must DIFFER per attempt (EC-6) so a crash can name a specific orphan; and it must NOT reach evidence, or every retry would look like a different analysis. Those are compatible only if it is metadata, never an input.
identityOwnership.contentDerivedIdentity: If a content-derived Run or Evidence identity is wanted, it is a SEPARATE identity computed from the sealed result — not the attempt anchor.

capabilityBoundary.why: B-R1V12-02 + R2-R1-02. Effectful ports reintroduce orchestration authority while the core is called pure.
capabilityBoundary.rule: DATA-ONLY CORE DEPS. The core never calls back out.

part1.scope: the core package, closed over CoreDeps
part1.forbidden: direct ambient imports or calls — filesystem, network, process spawn, clock, entropy, environment; and any effectful port (SnapshotPort, StorePort, ProviderPort, scheduler that creates threads/processes)
part1.permitted: reads of immutable value inputs already present in SealedStageInput and CoreDeps; pure in-memory budget meter mutations that cannot escape the evaluate call

part2.rule: Snapshot capture, provider execution, storage I/O and process supervision live in the host. Their authority is tested in host/adapter suites, never attributed to the pure core.

capabilityBoundary.honestLimit: Static closure over the pure core proves no direct ambient authority in that package. It does not prove host adapter confinement. Runtime denial of host authority is ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT / NOT DISCHARGED.

fields.rulesById: immutable map RuleId -> sealed rule artifact bytes/identity
fields.policyById: immutable map PolicyId -> sealed policy artifact
fields.resourceMeter: pure counter state for deterministic budgets declared in Plan
fields.diagnostics: bounded sink handle whose no-op form is observationally equivalent for evidence

coreDepsSchema.rule: Any field not listed is forbidden. CoreDeps is not an open extension point.

factoring.why: B-R1V12-03. v1.2's core API could not execute a full Plan — effectful fact-derivation and provider stages have no home in a pure core — so it either could not run, or relied on an unlisted orchestration authority that invalidated every lifetime-neutrality test.
hostExecutes: fact-derivation stages, including semantic providers and external scanners (C-2's supervised-implementation-effect class)
coreExecutes: rule-evaluation and policy-evaluation, which C-2 declares hold NO effect authority
factoring.interface: The host passes a SEALED StageInput / ObservationSet into the core. The core returns a CoreCompletion including policyOutcome. The core never calls back out and never seals a Run.
factoring.whyThisOne: It is the factoring C-2's effect taxonomy already implies: the stages with no effect authority are exactly the ones the pure core can run. The alternative — giving the core a typed supervisor port — would put effectful behaviour inside the boundary and make lifetime neutrality a property of the supervisor rather than of the core.
factoring.consequence: Lifetime neutrality is now a property of a component that genuinely could be resident or not, because it holds no resources either way.

suites.why: B-R1V12-04. One suite could pass lifetime-neutral core code without testing the host behaviour it claimed, while an unrelated storage failure could fail the core decision.

split.proves: multi-process integrity, busy timeout, byte-identical authoritative content

suites.rule: Suites are split by controlled subject. A failure in one suite may NOT be read as evidence about another. Cross-subject tests belong in composition-acceptance (R2-R1-05).

analysisBoundary.why: B-R1V12-05. v1.2 called the dependency set exhaustive while its instruments gave bounded evidence — the third recurrence of the absence-from-signature error.

instruments.detects: static reach through the package's own code

limits: dynamic dispatch and reflective loading are NOT fully covered by static closure
native code reached through FFI is covered only where binary inspection applies
an injected collaborator supplied by the host is outside the core's own closure by construction
analysisBoundary.rule: Unmodelled dynamic and native paths are TCB-ACCEPTED for included v1 code, or the dependent feature is excluded. They are NOT claimed as analysed or denied at runtime.
analysisBoundary.noExhaustivenessClaim: This artifact makes no exhaustiveness claim about the dependency set. It states which instruments ran and what each cannot see.

dischargeStatus.rule: implementable:true is feasibility metadata only. A property may be SPECIFIED by an implementable test declaration. DISCHARGED requires evidenceGrade DEMONSTRATED plus non-empty retained demonstrationEvidenceIds showing the test ran over its required domain and its negative control failed.
dischargeStatus.legacyFieldRule: For a property whose status is not DISCHARGED, dischargedBy is a legacy test-link field equivalent to specifiedBy; it is never assurance evidence.

coreCompletionSchema.why: B-R1V12-06. v1.2's return had no truthful value for cancellation, provider faults, missing Coverage, busy timeout or commit failure — so the core either lied or overstepped into host-owned sealing.

policyOutcome.rule: policy evaluation is core-owned; the host seals using this outcome and must not re-derive a different verdict from the same inputs

variants.note: deficiency uses the fact-plane vocabulary; policyOutcome.verdict is indeterminate when Coverage is incomplete
cancellation is a first-class outcome, not an exception

coreCompletionSchema.rule: The core NEVER seals a Run, publishes, or maps a termination. It returns a contribution; the host publication layer seals the authoritative Run and derives HostTermination (D9 TO-2/TO-3).

AttemptMetadata.rule: Injected, never minted. Excluded from EvidenceDigest by construction.

identityFixtures.why: two attempts sharing an ExecutionId make a crashed orphan unnameable (EC-6)
if the attempt anchor reaches the digest, a retry is incomparable to the original

completionFixtures.why: D9 TO-2: exactly one host-owned derivation and one write site

adjudicationRevision.note: Single pure-evaluation core boundary; data-only CoreDeps; policy outcome on completion; LN-12 cannot close findings; LN-10 composition suite; entropy removed; initial topology floor chosen.

initialTopology.normativeFloor: one-shot orchestration host + pure evaluation core

optionalResidentHost.constraint: A resident host is prohibited from changing EvidenceDigest, PlanId, Coverage semantics, or HostTermination relative to the one-shot floor for identical semantic inputs.
optionalResidentHost.measurementGated: Whether residency's measured benefits ever justify a later scope change remains a product decision; the v1 architecture contains no resident mode.

sharedBoundaries.host: admission, resolution, fact-derivation/providers, snapshot seal, storage publication, D9 mapping; Probe is future ontology only and excluded from v1
sharedBoundaries.core: rule-evaluation + policy-evaluation over sealed inputs -> CoreCompletion

initialTopology.weekOneDecision: Implement only the one-shot floor. Do not add resident mode behind a flag and do not invent a second evidence authority.
